thought_title: The great difference between Christians and people of the world
orientation: Macarius opens his homily by contrasting true Christians with people of this world, before urging believers to acquire the heavenly garment through faith and virtuous living.
pass_a_gloss: Great is the change between the Christians and the people of this world. For those who have the spirit of the world, in heart and in mind are bound in earthly bonds; but the others long for the love of the heavenly Father, having Him alone before their eyes with much desire. The world of the Christians is another, and their conduct, and mind, and word, and action is other, and the conduct, and mind, and word, and action of the people of this world is other. One thing are those, and another thing are these, and the difference is great between them. For the people of this world are bound in earthly bonds, but the Christians long for the love of the heavenly Father, having Him alone before their eyes with much desire. The world of the Christians is another, and their conduct, and mind, and word, and action is other, and the conduct, and mind, and word, and action of the people of this world is other. One thing are those, and another thing are these, and the difference is great between them.

choices.why: The noun denotes a shift or difference between two states; 'change' preserves the sense of a great alteration separating Christians from the world.
The second word is damaged but clearly parallels 'heart' as an inward faculty; 'mind' fits the context of inward bondage.
The verb expresses intense desire; 'long for' captures the yearning directed toward the Father's love.
The term refers to one's manner of life; 'conduct' is the glossary-consistent rendering for the Christians' distinct way of living.
The adjective marks the Christians' world as wholly other; 'another' preserves the stark contrast with the world of the people of this world.

pass_b_english: There is a great change between Christians and the people of the world. Those who have the spirit of the world are bound in heart and in mind to earthly bonds. But Christians long for the love of the heavenly Father, and they keep Him alone before their eyes with much desire.

The world of Christians is another world, and their conduct is another, and their mind is another, and their word is another, and their action is another. The conduct, mind, word, and action of the people of the world is other, and the conduct, mind, word, and action of Christians is other. Those people are one thing, and these are another. The difference between them is great.

The people of the world are bound to earthly things, but Christians long for the love of the heavenly Father. They keep Him alone before their eyes with much desire. The world of Christians is another, and their conduct, mind, word, and action is other.
notes: The source text contains extensive OCR damage and Latin-letter corruption in the latter portion; only the legible Greek clauses have been glossed. The damaged material appears to repeat and expand the opening contrast but cannot be reliably reconstructed.

problems.quote: Believers must strive through faith and virtuous living to acquire now the heavenly garment, because whatever glory the soul stores within will be revealed outwardly in the body on the day of resurrection.
problems.why: The source does not contain this claim; it appears only after the garbled text, not in section 5.
problems.fix: Remove this sentence or move it to the appropriate later section where it belongs.

problems.quote: The author uses the image of spring. After winter has passed, the trees are warmed by an invisible power from the sun and the winds, and they put forth leaves like garments, and flowers, and fruits. The flowers of the grass come forth from within the bosom of the earth. This is a type of the resurrection.
problems.why: No such spring imagery appears in the supplied Greek text for section 5.
problems.fix: Delete this paragraph or relocate it to the correct section where the spring metaphor occurs.

problems.quote: For true Christians, the resurrection day is like the first month, the month called April, which is the month called April. The glory of the Holy Spirit, hidden in their souls, will come forth and clothe their bodies. That Spirit will then be to them garment, food, drink, exultation, joy, peace, vine, and eternal life.
problems.why: The Greek passage for section 5 does not mention the month of Xanthicus/April, the resurrection imagery, or the list of gifts of the Holy Spirit.
problems.fix: Remove this passage; it belongs to a later section.

problems.quote: The Lord said that Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of the lilies (Matthew 6:29).
problems.why: The Lord’s saying is introduced in section 6 according to the brief; it should not appear in section 5.
problems.fix: Delete this sentence from section 5 or move it to section 6.

The author uses the image of spring. After winter has passed, the trees are warmed by an invisible power from the sun and the winds, and they put forth leaves like garments, and flowers, and fruits. The flowers of the grass come forth from within the bosom of the earth. This is a type of the resurrection.

For true Christians, the resurrection day is like the first month, the month called April, which is the month called April. The glory of the Holy Spirit, hidden in their souls, will come forth and clothe their bodies. That Spirit will then be to them garment, food, drink, exultation, joy, peace, vine, and eternal life.

The Lord said that Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of the lilies (Matthew 6:29). The glory of the Holy Spirit, hidden in the souls of the saints, will be revealed outwardly in their bodies on the day of resurrection. That glory will clothe them, and the Spirit will be their garment, food, drink, exultation, joy, peace, vine, and eternal life.
